questions.q: Machines E1, E2 and E3 produce 50%, 25% and 25% of tubes. Their defect rates are 4%, 4% and 5%, respectively. Which pair gives P(defective) and P(E1 | defective)?
questions.explanation: By total probability, P(D)=(1/2)(1/25)+(1/4)(1/25)+(1/4)(1/20)=17/400. Bayes theorem gives P(E1|D)=[(1/2)(1/25)]/(17/400). Simplifying the ratio gives 8/17.

questions.q: Plant X makes 70% of cars and plant Y makes 30%. Standard-quality rates are 80% at X and 90% at Y. A randomly chosen car is standard quality. What is P(X | standard)?
questions.explanation: The joint probability of coming from X and being standard is (7/10)(8/10)=56/100. The total standard probability is 56/100+(3/10)(9/10)=83/100. Dividing gives P(X|standard)=56/83.

questions.q: A fair die is thrown 10 times. A success is a score divisible by 3. What is the probability of at least 8 successes?
questions.explanation: A success is 3 or 6, so p=1/3 and q=2/3. The required binomial probability is C(10,8)(1/3)^8(2/3)^2+C(10,9)(1/3)^9(2/3)+(1/3)^10. Factoring 1/3^10 gives 45*4+10*2+1=201, hence 201/3^10.

questions.q: Let X be the number of heads in three tosses of a fair coin. What are Var(X) and the standard deviation of X?
questions.explanation: The distribution is P(X=0,1,2,3)=(1,3,3,1)/8, giving E(X)=3/2. Also E(X^2)=3, so Var(X)=3-(3/2)^2=3/4. The standard deviation is the square root of the variance, namely sqrt(3)/2.
